audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer tells the player to fire Electro Harpoon before Flamespitter. The kit's own E text is 'reducing their Magic Resist' and Rumble carries two harpoons.
audit.why: Both harpoons shred MR and Flamespitter is a 3-second damage-over-time cone, so every tick after the shred lands is amplified. Casting Q first and E after throws away the shred on most of the Q's duration. This is the single highest-value input the Rumble player controls in a lane where the trade maths is close.
audit.corrected: Land both Electro Harpoons first, then Flamespitter — the MR shred applies to every tick.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (E: reduces Magic Resist, 2 charges; Q: cone for 3 seconds)

audit.whatIsWrong: The text repeatedly frames Noxian Guillotine as something to survive but never says it is true damage, and the itemization advice elsewhere pushes resistances.
audit.why: Riot's R text is explicit: 'strikes a lethal blow, dealing true damage.' Magic resist and armour are both irrelevant to it. A Rumble who buys defensively expecting to live through the execute dies at the same health threshold he did before. Only raw health and distance change the answer.
audit.corrected: Noxian Guillotine is true damage — no resistance blunts it; only a health buffer and staying outside 460 range do.

audit.whatIsWrong: Overheat is described as a personal mistake ('overheat at a bad time') but never tied to the specific thing it costs you in this matchup.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: at 100 Heat Rumble is 'unable to cast spells for a few seconds'. Scrap Shield is Rumble's only disengage tool — he has no dash — and Apprehend is a 535-range pull. Reaching 100 Heat while inside pull range removes the shield and the harpoon slow at exactly the moment Darius needs you to have neither.
audit.corrected: Never reach 100 Heat inside 535 range: Overheat locks out Scrap Shield, the only answer to Apprehend.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early states Apprehend has a '24-second cooldown'. The packet also reports zero cooldown-sequencing cues in the whole matchup.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16. Rank 1 is 26s, not 24s. The entire matchup is built around whether that one button is up, so a two-second error on the wrong side is a real risk: a Rumble counting to 24 walks in while the pull is still live.
audit.corrected: Apprehend 26s at rank 1 falling to 16s at rank 5; Decimate 9s to 5s; Scrap Shield 6s flat at every rank; The Equalizer 130s at rank 1. Sequencing cue added: step inside 535 only after Apprehend whiffs.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early claims that 'at Level 2 he can E-pull into W-slow-Q for a crippling trade'.
audit.why: That is three abilities at level 2. Darius has two points spent at level 2, so Apprehend plus Decimate or Apprehend plus Crippling Strike, never all three. The full E-W-Q chain is a level-3 threat. Selling it as a level-2 pattern makes the player over-respect level 2 and under-respect level 3, which is when the combo actually arrives.
audit.corrected: At level 2 it is Apprehend into Decimate; the full pull-slow-Decimate chain is a level-3 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup is labelled diff 'FAVOURED' at diffRating 4/10 on a 49.56% win rate, and the two layers disagree about who wins the early levels: full.phases gives Rumble levels 1-4, while content.win and the packet level chart both give Darius levels 1-2.
audit.why: 49.56% over 1485 games is an even lane, not a favoured one. Worse, a player reading the level chart sees 'Darius' at level 1 and then reads the level-1 phase text telling him Flamespitter 'wins every melee level 1 — walk at them'. Walking at Darius at level 1 puts Rumble inside 535 pull range and inside Decimate's blade, which heals Darius. The two layers give opposite instructions on the most dangerous level in the lane.
audit.corrected: Difficulty restated as 5/10 at a 49.6% win rate; the level-1 and early-game text now says Darius owns levels 1-2 and that Rumble holds the outer edge of the 600 cone rather than walking in.
sources: champ-data/_kits/darius.json (E 535, Q heal on outer blade)

audit.whatIsWrong: content.spikes[2] calls The Equalizer a 'rocket wall' that he must 'eat or flash'. The kit file's derived flags also tag R (and Scrap Shield) as 'terrain'.
audit.why: The Equalizer is a damaging, slowing line of fire — it does not create collision terrain and does not block movement or dashes. A player who believes it walls Darius off will drop it as a barrier and then watch Darius walk straight through it into the kill. Scrap Shield is a shield plus a move-speed burst; the kit file's 'terrain' and 'knockup' flags on W are derived false positives with no support in Riot's own W text.
audit.corrected: Equalizer damages and slows across a line; it never blocks. Lay it across the retreat path so he eats ticks the whole way out.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (R: 'creating a wall of flames that damages and slows'; W: shield + speed only)

audit.whatIsWrong: report[6].t (Rune Setup) prescribes 'Arcane Comet, Manaflow Band, Transcendence, Scorch'.
audit.why: Rumble's resource is Heat. He has no mana bar, so Manaflow Band is a dead rune that can never trigger or stack — the player is running three effective runes in a four-rune tree. Nimbus Cloak or Nullifying Orb occupy the same slot and both do something on a manaless champion.
audit.corrected: Swap Manaflow Band for Nimbus Cloak in the Sorcery second row.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (resource: 'Heat'; every ability costType Heat / No Cost)']

audit.why: Executioner's Calling is an attack-damage item and cannot be built on an AP Rumble. The AP anti-heal line is Oblivion Orb into Morellonomicon. Naming an AD component as an option for a full-AP mage sends the player to the wrong shop tab against Darius, whose Decimate outer-blade heal is exactly what anti-heal is meant to answer.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal reads Oblivion Orb into Morellonomicon.
sources: champ-data/_kits/darius.json (Q heals off champions hit by the blade)

edits.before: Darius owns you at Level 1 and 2 — his passive bleed stacks from any Q chip damage, and at Level 2 he can E-pull into W-slow-Q for a crippling trade you cannot escape without flash. Do not Q-poke him from melee range before you have Heat control locked in; instead play for last-hits at the absolute edge of Flamespitter's cone and accept that these levels are survival, not dominance. His outer-ring Q heals him, so short back-and-forth trades feed his sustain while stacking your Hemorrhage — you need to be outside pull range or committing a full kite, never in the middle. If he burns Apprehend aggressively, note the 24-second cooldown; that window is yours.
edits.after: Darius owns you at Level 1 and 2 — his passive bleed stacks from any Q chip damage, and at Level 2 an Apprehend pull into Decimate is already a crippling trade you cannot escape without Flash. Do not Q-poke him from melee range before you have Heat control locked in; instead play for last-hits at the absolute edge of Flamespitter's 600-unit cone and accept that these levels are survival, not dominance. His outer-ring Q heals him, so short back-and-forth trades feed his sustain while stacking your Hemorrhage — you need to be outside pull range or committing a full kite, never in the middle. If he burns Apprehend aggressively, note the 26-second rank-1 cooldown; that window is yours.

edits.before: With double Electro-Harpoon online you can slow and sidestep Apprehend, but his Q heal and bleed sustain mean neither side reliably runs the other out — read the cooldown.
edits.after: Both harpoons shred his MR before Flamespitter lands, but Decimate's outer-blade heal and his bleed mean neither side runs the other out — trade on Apprehend's 26s, not on feel.

edits.before: Danger Zone Flamespitter matches his sustained trade, but 5-stack Noxian Guillotine still executes you if you mismanage spacing — these levels are skill-check, not free.
edits.after: Danger Zone Flamespitter matches his sustained trade, but Noxian Guillotine deals true damage — no amount of MR blunts it; only spacing and a health buffer keep you alive.

edits.before: Equalizer across his escape path forces him to eat the rocket wall or flash it — drop it perpendicular to the wave, not on his feet.
edits.after: Equalizer across his escape path makes him eat the burn line or Flash — it slows and damages but never blocks, so lay it across, not on him.

edits.before: Sustain Danger Zone Flamespitter through his outer-Q heal by trading short and stepping back before he stacks Hemorrhage
edits.after: Land both Electro-Harpoons before Flamespitter so the MR shred applies to every tick, then step back before he banks 3 Hemorrhage

edits.before: Flamespitter wins every melee level 1 — walk at them. Identify how Darius contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Darius owns level 1 — Decimate's outer blade heals off you. Spit Flamespitter from the cone's 600 edge and never step inside 535.

edits.before: Heat management is the kit: ride 50-100, never overheat by accident. Only take the trade when Darius's Apprehend is down.
edits.after: Ride 50-plus Heat for Danger Zone, never touch 100 — Overheat locks Scrap Shield, and the shield is your only answer to his pull.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Apprehend's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1 and 21s at rank 3 — a whiff hands you 20 seconds. Harpoon twice for the MR shred, then Flamespitter.

edits.before: - Darius Apprehend: matchup-defining — His all-in start. E-slow + kite. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Apprehend: 26s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — his only gap-close; step inside 535 range only once it whiffs. - Decimate: 9s to 5s. - Scrap Shield: 6s flat, save it for the pull. - Equalizer: 130s at rank 1.

edits.before: Flamespitter wins every melee level 1 — walk at them. Respect Darius's Apprehend completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Flamespitter outranges his blade, but never walk inside 535 — Apprehend starts every Darius kill. Levels 1-2 are about banking last-hits, not proving a point.

edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5/10 at a 49.6% win rate. The lane is decided by how well you track Apprehend and space it.

edits.after: Darius wins by landing Apprehend, stacking Hemorrhage to 5, and executing with true damage.

notes: Two corrections are champion-wide and the applier's exactly-once rule blocks them: (1) report[6].t Rune Setup prescribes Manaflow Band on Rumble, who is manaless (Heat) — 70 byte-identical copies across rumble.full.js, so it cannot be reached through a per-matchup proposal. It is a dead rune in every one of those 70 matchups and needs a structural fix. Nimbus Cloak is the natural replacement. (2) report[8].t Itemization offers 'Executioner's' as anti-heal — an AD item on a full-AP champion; the AP line is Oblivion Orb into Morellonomicon. Also blocked: full.diff ('FAVOURED') and full.diffRating ('4/10') contradict a 49.56% win rate, and every phases[].side/.rating is shared boilerplate, so the full layer still scores Rumble ahead at levels 1-4 while content.win and the packet level chart both give Darius levels 1-2. I corrected the phase *why* text to match the level chart but the side labels themselves are unreachable. Kit-file warning for whoever maintains _missing-interactions.json: Rumble's Scrap Shield is tagged 'knockup' and 'terrain' and The Equalizer is tagged 'terrain'. All three are derived false positives — Scrap Shield is a shield plus a move-speed burst with no displacement, and The Equalizer is a damaging, slowing line that does not block movement. Nine generated 'terrain-cuts-retreat' and 'knockup-enabler' entries for Rumble rest on those flags and should not be written into any matchup. what-kills-me.js was not touched.
